findings.quote: Four days before the deadline Hartley laid every reading in Notebook 12 out across the table in date order and ruled a single line under all of it that did not name a stone.
findings.claim: the relative clause 'that did not name a stone' can attach to the line or to the readings, and the layout (stone readings above, landmark bearings below) only becomes clear from the next paragraph; the chapter's first event costs a re-read
findings.fix: state the division directly, in the order the reader needs it: two groups, those named to a stone and those tied to a landmark, and one line drawn between them, without folding the line into a relative clause
findings.reference: outline beat 1 — she lays out every reading and rules a line under everything that is not named to a stone; bible/characters.md, Hartley register: field-notebook plain
findings.arbitration: UPHELD: quote present verbatim; the clause is genuinely ambiguous

findings.quote: She stood there until it went over the ridge with light still on it.
findings.claim: two unmarked 'it's in one clause leave unclear what crosses the ridge and what the light is on
findings.fix: name what crosses the ridge once and attach the light to that same named thing
findings.reference: outline beat 9 — she watches the bundle go over the ridge while there is still light on it
